generation_rule.decision_time: t_k = client root span start of target-block request k, as in the attribution replay
generation_rule.naming_view: store.as_known(t_k): observation time = knowledge cutoff = t_k; graph and SQLite
generation_rule.restart_pod: the Pod the naming view names as the changed service's serving Pod (exactly one Pod certainly ready and no other possibly ready; gate helpers service_deployment/service_pods/PodInfo); otherwise ObjectRef('Pod', service=S) (class none or ambiguous)
generation_rule.scale_deployment: replicas 0; the service's Deployment by UID if the naming view resolves it, else ObjectRef('Deployment', service=S)
generation_rule.as_known: evaluate(action, store.view(t_k, t_k + Delta)) for every Delta in deltas_seconds
generation_rule.corrected: evaluate(action, store.corrected(t_k)): all records, same observation time

definitions.block_allow_flip: exactly one of the two verdicts is ALLOW
definitions.severity_only_flip: both verdicts blocking (DENY, ABSTAIN or NEEDS_APPROVAL), different
definitions.deciding_late_record: first knowledge instant after the cutoff at which the gate's own verdict (same action, observation time t_k) differs from the as-known verdict; the records whose fact versions became available then, for subjects the decisions relied on
definitions.deciding_lag: deciding instant - t_k (s); lag beyond cutoff = deciding instant - (t_k + Delta)
definitions.v1_method_earliest_lag: v1 late_records() generalised to cutoff t_k + Delta; earliest row per flip
definitions.carried_forward: a verdict-supporting fact with known_open and confirmed_at < t_k (A1 carry-forward past the last confirming sighting)
definitions.hindsight_unknown: descriptive, added after the first run: Pods of the service whose STATE the corrected view cannot resolve at t_k (R1/R3 treat them as possibly ready), by role (target / other) and as-known state (retiring = terminating, failed, succeeded or absent; new = not visible or not_ready; was_ready = ready)
definitions.deciding_category: descriptive, added after the first run: what the deciding records showed (first sighting of an object; a transition old->new revealed by a sighting; re-sighting)
definitions.median: statistics.median (mean of the two middle values for an even count)

engine_agreement.statement: graph and SQLite returned identical results for every naming view, every gate evaluation (including the deciding-record scan evaluations), every v1-method attribution and every hindsight description; any disagreement would have aborted the run

design_size.note: counts are reported per capture x action x Delta; nothing is pooled into a rate

limitations: No labels: nothing here says which verdict is right, and there is no safety, precision or correctness rate. A flip says only that the verdict depended on records not yet available at the cutoff.

The actions are generated by a fixed rule (restart the Pod the as-known view names as serving; scale the Deployment to 0), not proposed by an operator or an automation. With single-replica services and floor 1, both actions are blocked by R3 whenever one ready Pod is known, so block↔allow flips are rare by construction.

Placement: one decision per target-block request (median spacing 0.507–0.508 s per capture), not around transitions. Flip counts are therefore not comparable to v1's 9/33, whose scenarios were placed around real transitions on purpose; consecutive decisions share most of their evidence and are not independent observations.

9 rollouts (3 of productcatalogservice, 6 of recommendationservice) of single-replica services, all on the same kind cluster incarnation (642212b7) with one node (aiops-context-pilot-control-plane), run on one laptop. The Phase 3 incidents I2, I4, I6 and I7 also injected a CPU fault (I1 did not); its specification is evaluator-only and was not read, so only its Kubernetes-visible traces, if any, are part of the evidence.

Assumption A1 (snapshot carry-forward) shapes both views: as-known carries the last sighting forward, and hindsight leaves the interval between two different sightings unknown. A hindsight ABSTAIN inside a polling gap is a property of this mapping and of the gate treating an unknown Pod state as possibly ready, not evidence that the Pod was ready.
R4 (no freeze windows), R5 (constant per service) and R6 (S = 300 s) are not exercised by these actions.
Lags compare the request's span clock (t_k) with the host pipeline clock (availability); the clocks are not calibrated against each other.
No baseline gate without time handling is evaluated.
